subject: Culture
title: Age and Respect
description: A short lesson to help you apply Age and Respect.

hook.text: In Korea, you must know someone's age before choosing how to speak to them. Grammar demands it.

buildup.text: Korean, Japanese, and Thai languages have built-in honorifics. The wrong form is a social blunder.

discovery.text: In the West, calling someone 'old' is offensive. In East Asia, age brings automatic authority.

twist.text: Silicon Valley worship of youth reversed the tradition. Tech culture prizes the young over the experienced.

climax.text: Whether age earns respect or irrelevance depends on the economy surrounding it.

punchline.text: Age is power in one culture and a burden in another.

quiz.question: Why must Koreans know someone's age before speaking to them?
options: To choose the right honorific level

details.summary: Age-based respect systems vary from reverence to relative indifference across cultures. Korean language has seven speech levels based on age hierarchy. Japanese seniority shapes workplace authority.
details.whyItMatters: Age-respect norms drive workplace dynamics, family structures, and social policy. Understanding them explains cross-cultural tensions around authority, innovation, and tradition.
takeaways: Korean language requires different verb forms based on age hierarchy
Japanese seniority system shapes promotions and decision-making
Western youth-focused culture increasingly marginalizes elders

faq.question: How does age hierarchy work in Korean culture?
faq.answer: Korean culture has elaborate honorific language levels determined by age. Even a one-year difference establishes a senior-junior dynamic. Older people eat first, drink first, and are served first.

faq.question: Why do Western cultures value youth over age?
faq.answer: Industrial capitalism shifted economic value from accumulated experience to innovation and adaptability. Technology acceleration made older knowledge obsolete faster. Youth-oriented marketing and media reinforced youth as the cultural ideal.
